beats.narration_en: How do you stop a runaway train at the end of the line?
Hitting a solid wall would wreck it, so this buffer stop is built to slide.
It's clamped to the rails by steel shoes, bolted on tight.
When a train hits, the stop's hydraulic buffers squash first.
Then the whole stop gets shoved along the rails, and the friction turns the train's speed into heat.
A six-car train at fifteen miles an hour stops in about sixty feet.
That's gentler than slamming on the brakes in your car.
Afterwards, crews loosen the bolts, push it back, and tighten them again.
